interactions.prompt: im doing a group assignment for uni and my part is object detection. we have a shared types file with an ObjectDetectionResult that my code has to return. where do i even start with this
interactions.response: Said to use a pretrained model rather than train one, since the assignment just wants a working baseline and training would take the whole time. Suggested torchvision's Faster R-CNN with COCO weights. Wrote the ObjectDetector class with a detect method that takes an image, runs it through the model, filters the output and returns it as an ObjectDetectionResult. Told me to add torch, torchvision and pillow to pyproject.toml.
interactions.humanIntervention: It used torch.no_grad() but didn't import torch at the top, so I added the import myself. It also assumed my detect function takes a PIL image when nothing in our shared types file specified that, I kept it but flagged the assumption to my group.

metaReflection.processEvolution: I started off asking pretty generally where to start and got a broad answer back. It got more useful once I asked about the actual file I had to fill in and the shared type it had to return.
metaReflection.criticalMoment: The code it gave me used torch.no_grad() but it forgot to import torch at the top, so I had to add that myself. It also decided my detect function takes a PIL image when nothing in our shared types file actually says that. I went with it but flagged it to my group instead of just assuming.
metaReflection.skillDependency: Knowing which pretrained model to pick and how to convert what the model spits out into the result type my team uses. I wouldn't have known where to start with either.
metaReflection.synthesis: Using a pretrained model was the right call for getting something working fast, but it meant I was using a model trained on real photos. That came back to bite me later when I found it doesn't classify simulator objects properly.
